clue.text: See 22
Titania's man in robe dancing about

indicators.note: dancing moves the letters of robe about into a new arrangement

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on (about) birds

explanation.surface: Someone spots Titania's husband twirling around in a robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' is the anagram signal; 'about' is the small word meaning regarding, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the fairy king is married to Titania, queen of the fairies.

clue.text: The writer, drunk outside hotel, an American

indicators.note: outside tells us the writer's letters go around the hotel's letters

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as me
an inn is a hotel
a sot is a drunk

explanation.surface: An inebriated author stands outside a hotel, and turns out to be an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' acts on 'The writer', which wraps the hotel, though the surface attaches it to 'drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Minnesotan comes from Minnesota, a state of the USA, so is one kind of American.

clue.text: Service provider quietly starting fires

indicators.note: starting places the quiet letter at the front of what follows

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical instruction to play quietly
arson is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: Someone who supplies a service is secretly lighting fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a church service, not a utility or a tradesman's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a clergyman who conducts church services, so he provides them.

clue.text: In US find amazingly silent pots and pans?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the letters US
amazingly suggests the letters of silent are thrown into a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Someone in America finds their cookware oddly quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' is the anagram signal and 'In' the container signal; 'find' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots and pans are examples of kitchen implements; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Henchman to talk too much?

definitions.meaning: to keep talking at tedious length

explanation.surface: A villain's heavy who never stops chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a thug employed for muscle, and going on means prattling interminably.

clue.text: Tree is what ripped cape

indicators.note: ripped means torn apart, so the letters of what are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: Cape Horn is the famous cape at the tip of South America, so horn can mean a cape

explanation.surface: A tree is what tore someone's cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped' turns WHAT into HAWT; a horn is a headland, as in Cape Horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn is a thorny shrub or small tree, common in hedgerows.

clue.text: Food store, being very low, reportedly delivers

parts.note: deep means very low, as a deep voice or deep water

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the one the clue gives

parts.note: frees means delivers, as in delivering from captivity

explanation.surface: A food store that is low on stock still delivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives FREEZE, which sounds like FREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-freeze is a freezer used to store food long-term at very low temperatures.

clue.text: Leader in congregation cut chat short

indicators.note: cut, with short following the word it acts on, signals a letter is removed

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is informal British for chatting at length
short says the cut comes at the tail end of the word, so the final letter is the one lost

explanation.surface: A congregation's leader interrupts some chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chatter; 'cut' and 'short' are one split indicator, cut short, removing the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi leads the worship and teaching of a Jewish congregation.

clue.text: Instrument has a light flashing outside Los Angeles

indicators.note: outside puts the light's letters around those of Los Angeles

parts.note: a strobe is a flashing light

explanation.surface: A device carries a lamp blinking around Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the light; 'outside' puts that light around Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old astronomical device for measuring the altitude of stars.

clue.text: This we can say about your underwear!

definitions.text: This we can say about your underwear!

parts.words: This we can say about your underwear!
parts.note: the front letter of the word your is Y, so the word your has Y as its front, and the briefs called by that name are men's underwear

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about the reader's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are British men's briefs with an inverted Y seam at the front; the word 'your' itself starts with Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Y-fronts are a style of men's underpants, so they could well be the underwear addressed.

clue.text: Workmen at last on street work uninterrupted

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word workmen

parts.note: op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: The workmen finally get onto the street and work without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-stop carries on continuously, without pauses or interruption.

clue.text: British burden to provide incentive

parts.note: an onus is a burden or responsibility

explanation.surface: A British obligation serves as motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra payment offered as an inducement or reward for performance.

clue.text: Those serving drinks here canned?

parts.note: bar staff stand behind the counter, while prisoners serving a sentence are canned, slang for jailed

explanation.surface: Where do the people pouring drinks work, if drinks come in cans?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' is both serving drinks and serving time; 'canned' is US slang for imprisoned (the can is a jail).
explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars is the idiom for being imprisoned, and literally where bartenders stand.

clue.text: One next door having love for daughter in New Edinburgh?

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the altered city name
having love for daughter means the letter for daughter is swapped for the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone living next door in a newly built Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping O for D in EDINBURGH gives EOINBURGH; 'New' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is the person living in the adjacent house.

clue.text: Ultra-conservatives in iron ships

definitions.meaning: ... stick rigidly to an uncompromising policy
ocean liners made of hard iron

explanation.surface: Right-wing extremists are found aboard ironclad vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardliners are people with unyielding, extreme positions; ironclad passenger vessels would be hard liners.

clue.text: Product required in unethical NHS era when poorly?

definitions.text: Product required in unethical NHS era when poorly?

indicators.note: poorly means in bad shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: If Britain's National Health Service went bad, you'd need private cover when sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's free state health service. 'poorly' rearranges UNETHICAL NHS ERA, and the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Health insurance is a financial product paying medical costs when someone falls ill.

clue.text: Cold War escalation with gun runners?

definitions.meaning: the USA and USSR competing to build weapons
read literally, guns running in a race

explanation.surface: A Cold War build-up involving weapons smugglers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gun runners' suggests smugglers, but read it as arms running a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The superpowers' competitive military build-up during the Cold War is called the arms race.

clue.text: Heads off for winter in pet surfing place

indicators.note: heads off means the first letter of each of these words is removed

explanation.surface: Someone leaves for a winter break, keeping their pet somewhere to surf.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading WINTER, IN and PET leaves INTER, N and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: People surf the web, so the internet is where online surfing takes place.

clue.text: Room at inn organised for one proposing candidate

indicators.note: organised means arranged in a new way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A room at an inn is set up for someone backing a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominator formally puts forward a person for election or appointment.

clue.text: See 22
Drink, tea to begin with, behind sandwiches?

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the late letters enclose the tea letter

parts.note: late means behind, as behind schedule

indicators.note: to begin with points to the first letter of tea

explanation.surface: A drink and tea first, then sandwiches after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the containment signal: LATE holds T.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a coffee drink made with espresso and steamed milk.

clue.text: Publication of which damaged party — and House — regret?

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A published document that harmed a political party and that Parliament came to rue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2022 Sue Gray report investigated lockdown parties at Downing Street ('Partygate'); 'damaged' rearranges PARTY HOUSE REGRET, and the surface hints at the scandal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil servant Sue Gray's inquiry findings were published as an official document, so the report is a publication.

clue.text: One stealing food sent back with reduced fat

indicators.note: sent back signals that the food's letters are read backwards

parts.note: grub is informal for food

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A diner returns their meal and asks for a lower-fat option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses GRUB into BURG; trimming LARD leaves LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is a thief who breaks into buildings to steal.

clue.text: Shelter king and Welsh emblem

parts.note: lee is shelter, as on the lee side away from the wind
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king takes cover beneath the national symbol of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is a national symbol of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: Caustic quip by well-mannered man?

parts.note: a pun is a witty play on words, a quip
a gent, short for gentleman, is a courteous man

explanation.surface: A cutting witticism from a courteous fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharply biting, just as caustic ones are; both are near-synonyms for acerbic.

clue.text: Fuss unduly about Democrat

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters for unduly enclose the letter for Democrat

parts.note: too means unduly, excessively
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: Making an excessive fuss over a politician from the Democratic party.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or a needless fuss.

clue.text: Court instrument always finding criminal

parts.note: a racket is used on a tennis or squash court
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A tennis racket is forever turning up a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, fitting 'criminal', but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a fraudulent or extortionate business, so is a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Drinks bought for mates — stout!

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for the whole group
stout as an adjective means plump, rotund

explanation.surface: Someone buys a pint of stout for the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the dark beer, but it is the adjective meaning portly.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying a round means paying for everyone's drinks; a stout person is round in figure.
